original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.

Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: On the paired-star schedule of open PR #7025, one internal matrix of rank at most q with P_s Z P_f = 0 has three core blocks of rank at most q, and the external thin rank is at least q(g-1). At g=31 and q=26 that is 780, which is 2q above q(g-3)=728. A sum of internal maps of rank greater than q is outside the claim.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. The assigned question is the second open question of open PR #7025: whether the three leaves met by one internal gap raise that paper's external bound above q(g-3). The consecutive bound of PR #7005 is not rerun, and a gap in every stage is not taken.
bottleneck_link: The g=31, q=26 profile passes the chronological floor 5q >= 4q+20 and is still unconstructed. PR #7025 separated one internal gap from total rank 130 by dropping three leaves, at external rank 728. Pricing those leaves for one rank-at-most-q matrix raises that external bound to 780. It does not change the selected frontier 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the sum of the three core-block ranks of one matrix of rank at most q. Do not build a word, do not treat an internal sum of rank greater than q as one rank-q matrix, and do not take a gap in every stage.
evidence: PROOF.md proves each of the three blocks has rank at most q under P_s Z P_f = 0, then the parity count R_ext >= q(g-1). verify.py checks the free-algebra block identities, the monomial support, an exhaustive F2 q=1 census, the explicit rank-q families, the stage-1 equality tuple, and a g=3 transport control. It prints PASS_INTERNAL_THREE_BLOCKS with external_rank 780 and dropped_leaf_rank 728. Python 3.12, standard library only.

open_questions.question: Can two matrices of rank at most q in the same internal gap, each with P_s Z P_f = 0, make every helped core block sum to rank 2q?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Rank 2q on each helped leaf would cancel the external remainder q and could return the external bound to q(g-3). This note stops at one matrix.
open_questions.first_step: Add two copies of the rank-q witness in PROOF.md on complementary core coordinates and read the three block ranks.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The one-matrix witness is already explicit.

open_questions.question: Does a gap-rank tuple of total q(g-1), together with one internal matrix of rank q, meet I_d on every core-to-leaf block at g=31, q=26?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The inequality count is sharp, but no word of external rank 780 is constructed. A word would show the bound is realized; a further obstruction would raise it again.
open_questions.first_step: At stage 1, place the rank-q witness in the internal gap and solve the even external gaps for a complement of its three blocks.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The equality tuple and the witness matrix are both in this package.
